messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: spike detected — /v1/generate 5xx rate up 6x, p95 latency > 2.5s, batcher_queue_length per-node trending upward for last 12m :rotating_light:

incident-bot: affected service=runtime-batcher, region=us-west1, impacted_nodes=3, symptom=OOMs & container restarts

sre-oncall: I'm paged, joining. pulling up node metrics and recent kube events.

alex: looking at logs from batcher-0/us-west1-a — seeing repeated `CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY` errors and `OOMKilled` from containerd. node kernel logs show repeated oom_killer events.

maria: we also see batch_accumulator length per-shard growing without bound. queue depth jumps then CPU and GPU memory climbs until process killed.

devon: can we throttle prefetch or disable kv-prefetch on the fly? that usually reduces memory pressure quickly.

zhen: running this now — toggling `REDWOOD_PREFETCH_ENABLED=false` on the runtime-config map for canary pods. applying to 2 pods in canary set first.

eliza: customer-ops — any customer impact noticed?

customer-ops: yes — 3 customers reported elevated 5xx and timeouts starting ~11:22 UTC, some requests returned `internal_server_error`. CS has reached out to one paying customer, they saw a batch timeouts that retried then failed.

sre-oncall: mitigation plan: 1) scale up dedicated batch pool by +2 nodes (temp) 2) disable kv-prefetch globally if canary looks good 3) lower `BATCH_MAX_TOKENS` from 8192->2048 4) drain and reboot OOMing nodes

alex: executing step 1 — spun up 2 new nodes (node-pool-batcher-extra). routing rule updated to include them.

zhen: canary updated — prefetch disabled on two pods, observing memory curve. so far for 3m memory stable and accumulator not growing.

devon: applying BATCH_MAX_TOKENS change now across batcher deployment. rolling update in progress. watch for latency regressions.

alex: sample error log from restarted pod:

```
2026-09-14T11:20:18Z runtime-batcher[pid=2134]: Allocating KV cache segment 128MB
2026-09-14T11:20:19Z runtime-batcher[pid=2134]: batch_accumulator.size=3128 requests
2026-09-14T11:20:19Z runtime-batcher[pid=2134]: cuda: cuMemAlloc failed -> CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY (err 2)
2026-09-14T11:20:19Z runtime-batcher[pid=2134]: fatal: couldn't reserve memory, aborting
kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 2134 (runtime-batcher) score 987 or sacrifice child
containerd: container "runtime-batcher" OOMKilled
```

maria: that matches the theory — continuous-batcher accumulation + aggressive prefetch => mem pressure => OOM. looks like eviction logic for long-tail requests isn't triggering because `request_id` TTLs are being extended by streaming responses.

devon: quick patch idea: clamp accumulator growth by enforcing `max_accumulator_requests = 1200` and drop/queue-shed older items when exceeded. I'll open a hotfix PR and we can cut a canary image.

eliza: agree. also recommend adding a runtime metric for `accumulator_shed_count` and an alert at >100/min.

alex: rolling restarts initiated on OOM nodes after drain. nodes are healthy again. no more container restarts in the last 4m on those hosts.

zhen: BATCH_MAX_TOKENS rollout done; memory graphs show immediate drop in usage across batchers. prefetch global toggle will go live in 2m after canary verification.

customer-ops: customers A and C asked for root-cause ETA. we should send a short update: we identified a batch-growth bug causing memory exhaustion; mitigations in progress (prefetch disable, batch size clamp, extra capacity).

sre-oncall: agreed. drafting: "We're mitigating a runtime batcher issue that caused OOMs in some nodes; mitigation includes disabling prefetch, reducing batch token limits, and adding capacity. We're monitoring and will follow up with a postmortem."

incident-bot: NOTE: SLA impact window 11:22–11:36 UTC — p95 latency > SLO, 5xx rate elevated.

devon: hotfix PR #4723 created — limits accumulator and adds safe-evict path. requesting expedited review from runtime-eng.

alex: can we do a quick canary deploy of the hotfix image?

maria: yes — canary deploy to 3 pods, then promote if stable for 5m. scheduling rollout now.

zhen: canary healthy at 3m. no regressions; accumulator bounded. promoting to prod, rolling update ongoing.

eliza: action items assigned: devon -> follow up PR tests + add metric; alex -> coordinate node reboots and monitor; zhen -> follow up on config toggle and revert plan; maria -> runbook update and postmortem draft.

customer-ops: will send customer update now with mitigation summary and ETA for final postmortem (24–48h).

sre-oncall: final status: mitigations deployed, metrics stable, no new OOMs in last 12m, closing pager. will schedule postmortem meeting. :white_check_mark:

maria: followup — add a recovery-mode safety test in e2e perf tests to simulate long-tail streaming requests + prefetch on to catch accumulation pathological cases.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED: runtime-batcher OOM spike contained. logs/alerts archived to /incidents/2941112222/artifacts.

eliza: thanks everyone. postmortem owner: maria. I'll link the timeline draft in #postmortems in 1h. :coffee:
